title: Dissipative controller as a hidden source of errors in quantum gates
authors: Serhat C. Kadıoğlu, Saulo V. Moreira, Mark T. Mitchison, Anthony Kiely
abstract: Quantum systems are typically controlled by classical devices that necessarily dissipate energy to the surrounding environment. By the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, this implies noise in the control field produced. We investigate the relationship between the resulting errors and the entropy produced by the macroscopic controller, working in the context of a concrete minimal model. In the most experimentally relevant regime of fast control and high fidelity, we find a tradeoff between dissipation and control errors. These findings are exemplified by perturbative calculations of the gate fidelity for simple gate implementations and of the fidelity of state transfer via shortcuts to adiabaticity in the Landau-Zener model. Our results quantitatively demonstrate that suppressing errors in quantum control typically comes at the cost of macroscopic dissipation, which is needed to tame fluctuations in the classical controller.
summary: This paper establishes a fundamental thermodynamic trade-off in quantum control, showing that reducing errors in quantum gates requires accepting a corresponding level of energy dissipation in the classical control electronics. By analyzing the relationship between gate fidelity susceptibility and entropy production, it provides quantitative bounds for designing energy-efficient and high-fidelity quantum operations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental trade-off between minimizing quantum gate errors and managing the unavoidable energy dissipation generated by the classical control apparatus.
main_result: It quantitatively demonstrates that suppressing quantum errors in control protocols necessarily incurs a cost in macroscopic dissipation within the classical controller.
method: The analysis uses second-order perturbative corrections to calculate gate fidelity susceptibility ($\chi$) and relates this error measure to the irreversible entropy production ($\Sigma$) of the classical circuit.
model_or_system: The system involves a quantum processor controlled by classical devices modeled as dissipative RL circuits. The Hamiltonian is time-dependent and perturbed by noise ($\delta g(t)$) originating from the controller's fluctuations.
key_observables: Gate fidelity susceptibility ($\chi$), Entropy Production ($\Sigma$), and the trade-off relationship between them.
important_parameters: Fast control regimes, high fidelity requirements, and the ratio of protocol time ($	au$) to noise correlation time ($	au_c$).
main_assumptions: The classical controller is treated as a dissipative system, and the error analysis relies on perturbative approximations valid under specific time/field strength conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic relationship between dissipation ($\Sigma$), noise ($\delta g$), and resulting infidelity ($\chi$) in the quantum system, and compare gate infidelity vs. dissipative cost for various gates.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by modeling the noise source, deriving the susceptibility $\chi$ from noise correlations, and then establishing the quantitative trade-off inequality linking $\chi$ and $\Sigma$ across various quantum control protocols.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the thermodynamic constraints on quantum computation, providing a quantitative link between the energy cost (dissipation) and the achievable fidelity of quantum gates, which is crucial for designing practical quantum hardware.
